findings.body:
chunk 1/3:

The added crossing test calls repositories directly; it never delivers input to an agent, sends a reply, reloads settings, or restarts a worker. The required end-to-end coverage for late arrivals, failures before versus after replying, two workers, settings reload, and restart is missing. Existing coverage does not establish this: apps/core/test/e2e/claim-protocol-two-process.postgres.e2e.test.ts:638–643 asserts the old cursor, and apps/core/test/agent-e2e/scenarios/boot-restart.agent-e2e.test.ts:114–143 verifies configuration survival. Add real-entry-point scenarios asserting delivery counts and persisted consumption. The review contract explicitly keeps missing tests at P1.
findings.title: Not done: No message is lost or given twice.

findings.body:
chunk 1/3:

These operations have no production callers, as intended for T1. Runtime admission still reads through getOrRecoverCursor and collectPendingMessagesSince (apps/core/src/runtime/message-loop.ts:497–509), and turn processing still reads the cursor (apps/core/src/runtime/group-processing.ts:96–108). Consequently, the storage addition alone does not deliver Done-when item 2. Its functional completion depends on T2's coordinated consumption/recovery switch and T4's runner delivery confirmations; track this as a dependency on those tasks.
findings.title: Later: T2 and T4 must complete message delivery and failure recovery

findings.body:
chunk 1/3:

The branch adds .factory/stories/TURN-1/**, plans/TURN-1.md, and plans/TURN-1.read.md, containing story-wide planning and historical review records. These paths are outside the permitted scope and are unnecessary to implement or test the storage contract. Move them to a separately scoped change. The port, integration tests, and canonical-message provider-account propagation are needed for this implementation.
findings.title: Remove story-wide planning and review artifacts from the scoped change

findings.body:
chunk 3/3:

The added concurrency test calls the repository through two connections, but never starts workers, reloads settings, restarts the runtime, or checks delivery to an agent. It therefore cannot detect messages dropped, replayed, or stranded across those lifecycle events. The existing two-process test at apps/core/test/e2e/claim-protocol-two-process.postgres.e2e.test.ts:140 races a job-run claim, and its recovery case at line 1038 checks lease fencing rather than message consumption. Add the required end-to-end consumption assertions, including failure before versus after a reply. Runtime wiring belongs to T2/T4, but the review contract explicitly keeps missing required tests at P1.
findings.title: Not done: Two-worker, settings-reload and restart message-consumption tests
